articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals for Supporting Iranian Petroleum and Petrochemical Sales
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026. These actions target individuals and entities involved in facilitating the sale of Iranian petroleum and petrochemical products, which are a significant source of revenue for the Iranian regime.

These designations aim to further disrupt Iran's ability to circumvent existing sanctions by targeting its illicit financial networks and those who provide material support to its energy sector. The move underscores the U.S. commitment to preventing Iran from using these revenues to fund destabilizing activities.

The specific individuals and entities designated were not immediately detailed in the initial announcement but are expected to be added to OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List).

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Sanctions on Cuban Sectors and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Issues Determination
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new cyber-related and transnational criminal organizations designations, alongside fresh Cuba designations on November 5, 2026. This action includes a determination paving the way for sanctions on the electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors of the Cuban economy.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the Trump Administration will not tolerate the Cuban regime funneling resources to its military elite, profiting from opaque offshore networks, or serving as a staging ground for hostile anti-American actors.

The broader sanctions package also targeted an oil shipping network, Cuban state-owned electronics and technical services enterprises, and individuals linked to the island's military-controlled economy.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities, Updates Listings, Issues Alert, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updates to existing Iran-related listings on November 4, 2026. Concurrently, OFAC published an Iran-related alert and issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question.

The Iran-related actions are part of the Trump administration's 'Operation Economic Outcast,' aimed at disrupting Iran's ability to fund its military and proxies through oil sales. The alert specifically highlights the substantial risk of designation or penalties for providing services to vessels using false flags to evade U.S. sanctions on Iran.
The amended Venezuela-related General License 60A authorizes transactions related to earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela, demonstrating a humanitarian carve-out amidst ongoing sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended General License for Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued Iran General License FF-1 on October 29, 2026. This amended general license authorizes the wind down of transactions involving the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.

This action provides a limited period for U.S. persons to conclude transactions with the specified entity, minimizing potential disruptions while maintaining the broader sanctions framework against Iran.

The issuance of such wind-down licenses is a common practice by OFAC to allow for an orderly cessation of business activities with newly sanctioned or identified entities, reducing unintended consequences for legitimate actors.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities for North Korea IT Worker Fraud and DRC Destabilization
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in North Korea's illicit IT worker fraud and those supporting destabilizing activities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Among the North Korea-related designations are individuals like Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov and Han Yu Song, both based in Russia, who are accused of leading and monitoring DPRK IT workers to generate revenue for the North Korean regime. The entity First Financial and Technical Development Center, located in North Korea and Vladivostok, Russia, was also designated for its role in financial and insurance activities supporting these illicit operations.

The DRC-related designations include the Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Zigama Credit and Savings Society for their alleged support of the M23 rebel group, which has contributed to the ongoing conflict and instability in eastern DRC.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, on October 27, 2026. Extreme Networks agreed to pay $1,529,685 to resolve nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks exported networking equipment and related services to Joint Stock Company Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer. MMZA was majority-owned by the designated entity JSC Concern Almaz-Antey, making it a blocked person by operation of law, even though MMZA itself was not directly listed on the SDN List until June 2022.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were voluntarily self-disclosed and egregious, highlighting the importance of thorough due diligence, especially in acquisitions and when dealing with third-party distributors in high-risk markets. A parallel investigation by the Department of Justice resulted in a non-prosecution agreement, with a portion of the OFAC settlement deemed satisfied by payments under that agreement.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amendments to several Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026. These updates pertain to the topics of blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.

The revisions, affecting FAQs 10, 32-36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53, are part of OFAC's ongoing process to review and ensure its published guidance remains current. While not introducing new sanctions programs or designations, these amendments clarify existing reporting mechanics and the distinction between blocking and rejecting transactions.

The updated guidance emphasizes the importance for financial institutions and other entities to correctly handle sanctions hits, including proper reporting procedures and the timely submission of blocked property reports and rejected transaction reports through the OFAC Reporting System (ORS).

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran and Russia-Related General Licenses, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026. Concurrently, OFAC also issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions.

In a separate action, OFAC also announced the removal of certain Belarus and North Korea designations. This indicates a dynamic approach to sanctions, with both new restrictions and targeted removals occurring based on evolving foreign policy considerations.
The specific details of the new designations, general licenses, and removals were not immediately available but are expected to be published on OFAC's website.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Chinese Entities Under PAIPA, Issues Associated General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026. In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued PAIPA General License 1, 'Transactions Authorized Pursuant to the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations,' and PAIPA General License 2, 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving Certain Entities Blocked on October 19, 2026.'

Several Chinese entities were added to OFAC's Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions List (NS-MBS List), including BEIJING QIJI CHUANGTAN PHASE I VENTURE CAPITAL CENTER LIMITED PARTNERSHIP (a.k.a. MIRACLE PLUS RMB FUND I), BEIJING QIJI CHUANGTAN PHASE II VENTURE CAPITAL CENTER LIMITED PARTNERSHIP, and BEIJING QIJI CHUANGTAN ZHIYUAN ENTERPRISE MANAGEMENT CENTER LIMITED PARTNERSHIP.

These designations impose various restrictions, including the blocking of property, prohibitions on loans from U.S. financial institutions exceeding $10,000,000 in any 12-month period, and prohibitions on foreign exchange and banking transactions. The actions underscore the U.S. government's focus on protecting American intellectual property and countering cyber-related threats.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Venezuela-related General License 60A on October 16, 2026. This license specifically authorizes transactions related to earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela.
In addition to the amended General License, OFAC also issued one amended Frequently Asked Question, FAQ 1263, to provide further clarity and guidance on the authorized activities.
This action highlights OFAC's continued efforts to provide humanitarian exemptions within its sanctions programs, allowing for critical aid to reach the Venezuelan population in times of need.

body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) to settle nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

The violations involved the export of networking equipment and related services to a Russian defense manufacturer, Joint Stock Company Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), which was majority-owned by a designated entity and thus blocked by operation of law.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were voluntarily self-disclosed and egregious, emphasizing the importance of robust sanctions compliance programs, particularly in identifying ultimate beneficial ownership and managing risks associated with third-party distributors.

articles.headline: Global Markets React to Midterm Election Results and Geopolitical Tensions
body: Global financial markets are showing mixed reactions following the U.S. midterm elections, which saw significant gains for the Democratic party, winning control of both houses of Congress. Investors are closely watching how the new political landscape will influence fiscal policy, particularly in areas such as trade and government spending.

Geopolitical tensions, especially concerning the ongoing conflict in Iran and its impact on oil prices, continue to be a major factor influencing market sentiment. The U.S. Treasury's 'Operation Economic Outcast' against Iran, coupled with rising inflation rates in Iran, is contributing to uncertainty in energy markets.

Analysts suggest that the shift in congressional control could lead to a re-evaluation of current foreign policy strategies, potentially impacting global trade relations and commodity prices in the coming months.

articles.headline: U.S. Sanctions Indian and Turkish Firms for Aiding Iranian Oil Evasion
body: The U.S. Treasury Department issued fresh sanctions on November 4, 2026, targeting companies and individuals based in India and Turkey for their alleged support of Iran's efforts to evade sanctions. This action is part of the Trump administration's 'Operation Economic Outcast,' which aims to cripple Iran's ability to fund its military through oil sales.

The sanctions specifically target a 'vast criminal network' led by India-based Suniel Kumar Sharma, his wife Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, and other Indian citizens, along with nine associated entities. These individuals and entities are accused of providing false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum.

Additionally, Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc was sanctioned for its ongoing support of Iran's heavily sanctioned aviation industry. The U.S. warned that it would continue to pursue anyone supporting the Iranian government's illicit activities.

articles.headline: U.S. Sanctions Chinese Firms for Alleged Military Supplies to Cuba
body: The United States has imposed sanctions on two Chinese companies, China National Electronic Import and Export Company (CEIEC) and Beijing H&C Technologies, accusing them of supplying equipment and components to Cuba's military. This move intensifies Washington's pressure on Havana's foreign suppliers and expands its authority to target businesses operating on the island.

The U.S. State Department stated that these companies collaborated with Cuban arms procurement company Sociedad Mercantil Duna to provide military-related goods in 2026. Secretary of State Marco Rubio asserted that Cuba's foreign backers are sustaining its armed forces and enabling repression.

In a parallel action, the Treasury Department expanded the sectors of Cuba's economy subject to sanctions to include electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology. This determination, effective from November 5, 2026, opens the door for further designations of foreign businesses, regardless of nationality, operating in these sectors.

articles.headline: Revisions to the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) revises the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List under the destination of China, People's Republic of (China). This determination follows the removal from the Entity List of Arrow China Electronics Trading Co., Ltd., and the removal of six aliases for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. in November 2025.

articles.headline: Removal From the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing one entity from the Entity List under the destination of Turkey.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: OCC Imposes $750 Million Assessment Against Bank of America for Deficient BSA/AML Compliance
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today announced a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, N.A. (bank), for violations of the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, including 12 CFR 21.21 and 12 CFR 21.11. This amount is the largest in OCC history.
